name: Chant Wizard
disclosure:
We are an independent game studio. The visual effects in the game’s videos and animations were created using an AI-assisted rendering pipeline, primarily to enhance the presentation of special effects, magic, and fantasy scenes.
The game’s concept art, compositions, lighting, storyboards, and overall art direction were all designed by our team. For some scenes, our artists first completed the 3D modeling, materials, and lighting before using an AI-assisted pipeline for stylized rendering and post-processing. AI was used solely as a visual production tool, and all related content was designed, selected, refined, and reviewed by our team.
All art assets in the game were either created by our team or used with proper authorization. We hold all necessary copyrights and usage rights, and all assets comply with applicable laws and regulations. Every asset also reflects the time, dedication, and creative effort of our team.
The game’s core gameplay and systems were independently designed by our team. Our voice cast includes professional actors who have worked on titles such as DYNASTY WARRIORS: ORIGINS and Black Myth: Wukong, as well as several content creators and streamers.
This game is a heartfelt gift from us to wizards everywhere. We hope you enjoy exploring its magical world!

disclosure:
Ammerow: Lands Beyond was developed with substantial AI assistance under human direction, selection and review.
The music was created with Claude Compose, a bespoke composition system built for this project. Anthropic’s Claude assisted by writing and running code that arranges melody, harmony, counterpoint and orchestration note by note. The compositions were rendered using licensed virtual instruments in Ableton Live, then analysed and refined. No generative-audio or generative-music model was used. Every piece was directed, reviewed and approved by a human.
The sound effects are an original, human-directed procedural synthesis library. Claude Code assisted in writing custom Python digital-signal-processing software and individual cue recipes. Waveforms were deterministically rendered from mathematical models and recorded seeds. No recordings, performers, samples, stock audio, sample libraries or generative-audio service were used to create the effects.
Ammerow is designed primarily as a coloured ASCII game. Detailed creature, item and shopkeeper illustrations began as AI-generated source images, selected and reviewed under human direction, then converted through a deterministic ASCII-art pipeline.
The optional Hybrid presentation offers 32×32 and 64×64 sprites made by cropping and sampling those same source illustrations. Neither conversion process uses additional image generation, but both retain their AI-generated source provenance. Terrain and subjects without sprite bindings use ordinary ASCII glyphs; inspection cards and shopkeepers retain their ASCII illustrations. No inherited Angband tilesets are included.
Some narrative, gameplay data and other player-facing material were developed with AI assistance under human direction and review. AI coding assistants also contributed to the game’s software and production tools.
Some Steam marketing backgrounds were created using OpenAI image-generation tools, then selected, reviewed and combined with deterministic Ammerow branding by the developer.
All AI-assisted content is prepared in advance. The game does not generate content using AI models or connect to AI services during gameplay.

name: Aika Was Supposed to Die
disclosure:
Hi everyone. I want to be open about how this game was made and why generative AI was used.
Aika Was Supposed to Die began as a story that I wrote and developed over more than two years. The world, characters, dialogue, themes, and narrative direction were all written by me. I cared deeply about this story, and eventually I felt that a visual novel would be the best way to bring it to life.
As an independent developer working with a limited budget, hiring a full team of artists is not financially possible for me right now. I greatly value human-made art and the work of professional artists. I am also a 3D artist who works with Unreal Engine, so this is something I genuinely care about.
Rather than leave the story untold, I chose to use generative AI as part of the visual production process. The game’s images and video assets were created with the assistance of generative AI tools. However, I did not want that to become an excuse for delivering something careless or low-quality. In fact, having access to these tools encouraged me to be as ambitious as possible with the project.
I created and refined a large number of images and animated sequences to give the game a richer and more cinematic presentation. Every asset was carefully directed, selected, edited, revised, and manually integrated into the story, with the goal of providing players with a cohesive, polished, and emotionally engaging experience.
The writing, narrative design, scene direction, timing, editing, and final creative decisions were all handled by humans. Generative AI was used as a production tool, not as a replacement for authorship, creative direction, or care. No AI content is generated during gameplay.
If the game becomes successful enough to support a larger production, I would love to work with professional artists on future chapters. Until then, this approach has allowed me to share a story that means a great deal to me while doing everything within my reach to make the final experience cohesive, personal, and emotionally meaningful.
Thank you for giving this story a chance.

disclosure:
As an individual developer, during development of this game, AI tools were heavily used. I disclose this honestly and transparently.
1. In-Game Assets
Illustrations & Art: Unit portraits and the opening cinematic illustrations were generated using AI image models, then manually curated, retouched, and unified in style. All assets were human-reviewed under strict art direction to ensure historical tone and consistency.
Opening Cinematic: Subtle motion effects on the illustrations were produced with an AI image-to-video model and assembled by using the Remotion pipeline.
Background Music: The soundtrack was generated by an AI music model in multiple takes, then human-selected, mixed, and mastered.
Telegram Voice-overs: The  historical telegram voice-overs in-game were synthesized by an AI TTS system. Each character's reference voice was human-approved through listening tests before use.
2. Development Assistance
Code: Game code was written and debugged with the aid of AI coding assistants. All code was human-reviewed and validated through automated testing.
Localization: The game supports Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English. The English text was AI-drafted and human-proofread.
3. What Is NOT AI-Generated
Historical Text: The telegrams in-game are taken from historical archives, 34 are verbatim transcriptions of the original documents, and 12 were written based on the sources. They were not AI-generated.
Terrain & Map: The battlefield map was procedurally rendered from real elevation data (SRTM), not generated by AI.
Game Balance & Statistics: Troop strength, Unit Introduction, and values were researched and set manually from historical sources, cross-checked for accuracy and play balance.

AI is used at runtime to evaluate a player's drawing, chosen creature name and language, and to generate the creature's element, stats, moves and descriptive text. Drawings are sent through our Cloudflare-hosted service to the DeepSeek API for evaluation and content moderation; chosen names and language settings are sent for evaluation. Ghost Sharing also sends each creature’s drawing, party text fields and the in-game display name for content moderation. The player's drawing remains the creature's artwork. Private friend matches using an existing party also send creature drawings, party text fields and the in-game display name to the DeepSeek API for content moderation.
Player-created drawings, names and generated text can be shown to other players when a player chooses Ghost Sharing or enters an online match. Ghost teams may appear as asynchronous opponents and in the stamp ranking. Real-time friend matches use private rooms joined through a room code or Steam invitation, using an existing team or creatures drawn during an Instant match. This release has no public/random real-time matchmaking. Participating in a match does not by itself publish a creature as a shared ghost or add it to the public ghost ranking.
The service applies automated content moderation and blocks content it rejects from the corresponding registration or sharing flow. Players can report content through the official website's contact form. Automated moderation can make mistakes. Battle outcomes are calculated by deterministic game rules, not by AI.

name: EQUILIBRIUM
disclosure:
EQUILIBRIUM uses generative AI to power its core gameplay mechanic: the Policy Terminal.
LIVE-GENERATED CONTENT
When a player types a directive or law in natural language (e.g., "Abolish the luxury car tax"), the AI Engine analyzes the request in real time and generates a structured governmental dossier, including:
- Legislative feasibility analysis
- Budget impact and financial coverage
- Macroeconomic effects (GDP, debt, inflation)
- Social and political consensus projections
- Parliamentary vote simulation
Model used: Anthropic Claude, accessed via API.
Guardrails: AI output is constrained to a fixed set of structured fields defined by the developer. All numeric effects are clamped within bounds enforced by the simulation engine, so no AI output can produce values outside the game's defined ranges. The model operates only on the simulation state provided to it and cannot invent game data: commands that cannot be mapped to a valid government action are refused, and the player is offered bounded policy alternatives instead. No image, audio, or user-data generation is involved, and no player data is used to train any model.
Because responses are generated at runtime, outputs vary between playthroughs: the same directive may produce different wording and different outcomes.
PRE-GENERATED CONTENT
The game's background music track was generated using AI tools during development and ships with the game.

disclosure:
I'm not a professional game developer or artist. Making my own game had been a dream for years, but I never knew how to turn that dream into reality. Generative AI became the tool that finally made it possible.
With its help, I created many of the game's visual and audio assets, including item, UI, skill, and module icons, character portraits, ships, space stations, backgrounds, the game icon, the Steam store artwork, and some of the sound effects. It also assisted me with programming.
But Star Corsairs is not a game that AI simply generated. Every asset was reviewed, rejected, refined, or replaced until it matched the vision I had in mind. Every gameplay system was designed, tested, and reworked repeatedly until it felt right. The economy, ship balance, pirate AI, combat, and progression were all shaped through countless hours of playtesting and manual iteration. The story, world, and all of the writing were created by me.
Without generative AI, this game would probably never have existed. But without the countless creative decisions, revisions, and work behind every part of it, Star Corsairs wouldn't exist either.

I'm an ordinary gamer who has played games for almost twenty years and always dreamed of making one of my own. But I can't write code, and I've never been trained in art or music. This game exists because generative AI filled those gaps for me: parts of the code were written with the help of AI coding tools; some character, environment, and UI art was created with image-generation models, then hand-picked and adjusted by me; some animation, music, and sound effects were also made with AI tools.

name: 励ます信長
disclosure:
This game lets you converse with a character based on the historical Japanese warlord Oda Nobunaga. The character's reply text is generated on the fly by a language AI that runs locally on your own PC in response to your input.
・Everything runs entirely on your PC. No data is sent to any external server, and the game works without an internet connection.
・A system prompt (character definition) keeps the AI in role: speaking in Nobunaga's style and offering encouragement. It answers based on the historical record and will honestly say it doesn't know when it doesn't.
・The only thing generated at runtime is conversation text. The portrait uses a public-domain painting, and the talking and blinking animations based on that portrait are fixed clips created with a video-generation AI during development and played on a loop. Speech is produced by a voice-synthesis engine (VOICEVOX).
・This is a conversational app made for encouragement and light counsel. The AI's responses vary every time and are not guaranteed to be accurate. Please enjoy it as entertainment.

tags: Strategy|Board Game|Singleplayer|Online Co-Op|Turn-Based Tactics|Fantasy|Dark Fantasy|Co-op|Tactical|Local Co-Op|Indie|Tutorial|Top-Down|Local Multiplayer|Multiplayer
disclosure:
Scourge of the Necromancer makes significant use of generative AI in its production. We want to be fully upfront about it.
Visual assets (2D images + video) — all AI-generated, then human-curated and human-edited. Every shipped image and video in the game and on the Steam store page was produced with AI tools, then reviewed, edited, and selected by hand by the developer. This covers: Steam store capsules and library art, the store-page background, all in-game achievement icons, hero portraits, the Necromancer concept art, decorative UI elements, all real-time cinematics (the defeat sequence and all victory variants), and the marketing trailer's atmospheric segments. Image models used: Google Imagen 4, Google Veo 3.1 (video), Nano Banana Pro / Gemini 3 Pro Image (Google), Black Forest Labs FLUX.2, Recraft V4 Pro, Ideogram V3, and Bria RMBG-2.0 (background removal). Final assets received human editing — compositing, color correction, retouching, frame extraction, masking, and rejection of unusable outputs.
3D models — AI-generated base meshes, then human-edited in Blender. The in-game hero character models (Knight, Cleric, Ranger, Wizard, Warrior, Alchemist) started as outputs from Tripo AI's generative 3D model service (FBX + texture PNGs), but each model was then opened in Blender by the developer for hand editing — mesh cleanup, geometry adjustments, and texture fixes — before being exported for use in the game. Each finished model was imported into Unity with hand-tuned scale, rotation, material configuration, and import-setting curation. Unsatisfactory generations were discarded and re-prompted; the Blender editing step is substantial enough that the shipped models are not pure AI output.
Music — AI-generated, then human-curated and post-processed. All music tracks in the game (menu, gameplay layers, boss phases, victory, defeat) were produced with Google Gemini's music generation, then human-selected, trimmed, looped, and mixed by the developer.
Necromancer voice — AI-generated, then human-edited. The Necromancer's spoken syllables were synthesized with ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech (Eleven Multilingual v2 model), then pitch-shifted, EQ'd, and processed with reverb in Audacity by the developer to produce the final in-game delivery. No other character has spoken voice lines in the shipped game.
Sound effects — all AI-generated. Every SFX in the game (ability sounds, ambient layers, UI sounds, footsteps, kill/spawn cues, tile state cues, boss audio) was produced with ElevenLabs Sound Effects, then human-selected, trimmed, processed, and mixed by the developer. The Necromancer voice lines use ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech (covered separately above).
Runtime behavior. The game does NOT use live-generated AI content at runtime. Every shipped asset is a fixed, pre-rendered file. Player-facing text, dialogue, narrative, lore, and game design were written by the developer without AI generation.
Code. Code development used Claude (Anthropic) as an AI coding assistant. This is behind-the-scenes efficiency tooling not consumed by players, but we mention it here for full transparency.

name: AI Slop
disclosure:
Warning: This game contains trace amounts of human effort—mostly restricted to pressing "Ctrl+C" and "Ctrl+V."
In the spirit of our title, "AI Slop" was created using generative artificial intelligence for practically every asset, line of code, and marketing material in existence.
Here is exactly how we let the machine do our jobs:
- Art & Assets: Every single visual asset, from the UI to the 6-fingered anime girls and the melting hands of our characters, was generated using text-to-image AI tools. No digital painters were harmed in the making of this game, because we didn't hire any.

A note on AI-generated content

﻿
There is no fixed script. No predetermined ending. You type — and the AI writes the next scene.

﻿
Launch the game, click Start, and an opening scene is generated instantly. From there, choose from suggested options or type your own response freely. The AI director crafts each turn: dialogue, character emotion, scene atmosphere, and a matching anime-style CG illustration — all in real time.
﻿
✨ Features
﻿
∙ Truly Infinite Stories Every playthrough is different. The AI generates dialogue, plot twists, and character moments on the fly — no two sessions will ever be alike.
﻿
∙ Anime CG Illustration Each scene is paired with a freshly generated visual novel-style illustration. Characters maintain a consistent appearance throughout your story.
﻿
∙ Custom Character Cards Import SillyTavern-compatible character cards (PNG) to play with your own characters — complete with custom personality, backstory, scenario, and opening lines.
﻿
∙ Save & Load System Save your story progress at any point and pick up right where you left off.
﻿
∙ Bilingual Support Switch seamlessly between Chinese and English. Story content, UI, and AI output all adapt to your chosen language.
﻿
∙ Optional AI Voice Characters can speak their lines aloud with AI-generated voices matched to their gender, age, and personality.
﻿
∙ Safe & Moderated Built-in multi-layer content safety: keyword filtering on both input and output, AI self-review on every response, and a one-click in-game report system.
﻿
📝 Note Infinite GalGame requires an internet connection to generate stories. Content is produced by AI and may occasionally be imperfect — use the in-game report button to flag anything unusual.

name: Human Error
disclosure:
Human Error utilizes cloud based generative AI to power the dialogue and interrogation systems of its robotic characters. During the Debrief Session, an integrated model generates text responses based on your performance metrics in the preceding tasks. This technology is used to create dynamic, unscripted confrontations where the machines analyze your behavior and react to your input in real time.
The game generates text-based dialogue during the social deduction phase. This content is created in real time using your performance data (movement patterns, task efficiency, and error logs). This process requires an active internet connection to communicate with our cloud hosted AI systems. We have implemented guardrails to ensure the AI remains within the thematic boundaries of the game.

Every background is rooted in reality. Our team personally traveled to each location for on-site photography. disclosure:
AI-Generated Content Disclosure
I am a solo developer with no programming background. Before using AI, I spent three months following YouTube tutorials, deleted everything and restarted three times, and typed every line of code myself until the foundation of this game clicked.
From there, I used AI — primarily Claude — as a teacher and debugging partner across 7,000+ conversations over 16 months to learn GDScript and build every system in the game. The first line in my prompts is always "Stop being a yes sayer and always be brutal and honest."
Here is exactly what AI was and wasn't used for:
Code: I spent my first three months writing every line of code by hand. As the project grew, AI became a development partner — drafting code from my descriptions, which I then reviewed, debugged, and integrated. AI taught me programming concepts and helped me solve problems. Every design decision and system architecture is mine.
Art: AI-generated with extensive human direction and manual editing. Some pieces required 15 pages of descriptions. I often assemble final art from multiple elements — finding references, combining parts, and making hands-on edits until it matches my vision.
Animation: The first 14 enemies and 2 bosses were animated by me personally in DragonBones. For newer content, I'm exploring AI-generated animations and working to make them feel personal and consistent with the game's style — you can see examples with the later bosses. Some of these I'm still not satisfied with and will redo, which is just part of the process.
Music: I produced 350+ tracks using AI music tools and curated the best for the game. All creative direction — mood, style, placement — is mine.
Writing: All card text, lore, descriptions, and UI text are written by me. AI occasionally helps with polish.
Game Design: Every mechanic, card interaction, and balance decision comes from a lifetime of gaming — hundreds of board games, decades of Magic: The Gathering, a career at Blizzard Entertainment, and more consoles than most people can count. AI does not design games. That part is entirely human.
EDIT1: I felt the need to mention that I got diagnosed with ADHD last year, at the age of 47. The reason I could never learn coding in a traditional way is my attention span. If I am not interested it is super hard, and if I am interested it is super awesome. I get excited when I can talk and describe how I want my game to feel and function. The AI converts that to code, and together we've created a way for me to follow my dream and make a game that I want to play. I have thought to myself many times during development that I wish I knew how to make this myself, and I wish I was able to just learn and do things like most people. But here we are.
"EDIT2: I updated the Code section to be more precise. I only wrote code entirely by hand for the first three months. After that, AI and I worked together — I designed and described what I needed in detail, AI drafted it, and I reviewed, debugged, and integrated everything."

We integrate artificial intelligence solely as a creative assistance tool during pre-production and artistic exploration phases.
Specifically, we use image generators to produce preliminary concept art, explore different visual directions, and accelerate iteration on our graphic ideas.
AI serves only as a source of inspiration, while the entire final content is fully created, curated, and refined by our human team.
Generated images are never used as-is in the final product.
Every visual element in the game (textures, characters, environments, illustrations, etc.) is recreated, retouched, painted, recomposed, or manually validated by our artists to ensure:
originality of the content,
respect for copyright,
artistic consistency,
and compliance with Steam/Valve guidelines.
AI does not contribute to the generation of final assets, 3D models, animations, sounds, or any other elements directly integrated into the game.
Its role is strictly limited to providing visual references, aesthetic guidance, and starting points to help our team work more efficiently.
This approach allows us to maintain a strong and authentic artistic identity while benefiting from a more fluid, inspiring, and innovative creation process — directly reflected in the quality, coherence, and originality of our game.

disclosure:
AI generative models were used to create localization files to support languages that would otherwise be difficult for a solo developer. Placeholder AI-generated assets have been created for the Steam store splash images, with the intent of commissioning an artist if this gains community support. All in-game assets (sprites, music, sound effects, UI elements, and interactive content) were created by humans and are credited in the game credits. CPU opponents use traditional game AI algorithms, not generative AI models.
This is the third iteration of development, that was originally developed in 2019 with HTML + JS, then rebuilt in Unity, and then transferred to LOVE2D written in Lua. It was more-or-less built with a box of scraps in a cave in its first iterations, and modern software since those days have effectively blurred the line where task automation meets unethical AI consumption.
It's up to each of us to determine where that line is for ourselves in a rapidly changing digital age. As both a solo game dev and multimedia artist carrying a full-time job in neither of those fields, I feel that it's important to be educating ourselves on where AI can be a useful tool to allow new opportunities and expand capabilities for independent creators that are otherwise untenable, while keeping the human side of game dev at its core, especially in the indie genre.

The procedure is as follows:
Based on detailed world-building settings, prompts are created and input into Dall-E 3 to generate images multiple times.
A single output image—or a combination of several output images—is then used as a reference sketch to create pixel art.
In addition, except for some parts, the map background images are also generated by creating prompts from the world-building settings and inputting them into Dall-E 3. The resulting images are then used as reference sketches to produce pixel art.
By following this method, while we leverage AI-generated images, the final designs are all completed as pixel art by human hands.

name: Rooster Saga: I Believe I Can Fly
Tobiano
tags: Simulation|Horses|Casual|Management|Sports|Open World|RPG|Inventory Management|Character Customization|Crafting|Nature|Immersive Sim|Realistic|Early Access|Indie|Strategy|Animation & Modeling|Game Development|Farming Sim|Third Person
disclosure:
As the AI debate continues to evolve I feel the need to add nuance to this statement so players can make an informed decision whether or not to support human game developers.
I took 5 years of classes learning code and 3D to produce my game.  When the AI boom hit, Tobiano was already a functioning breeding and management simulator.  At my day job, we were encouraged to use AI for everything from image generation to writing emails.  I opposed the use of AI for creative aspects and human communication, but tested out chatbots for help with code.  Problems solved with AI include things like "how do i make the camera follow the player".  A lot of the problems ended up more convoluted by AI.
Most of the code written early in the game has gone through 2-3 iterations to simplify and be easier to work with and debug. For example, the riding lesson system was redone completely after the first 5 lessons were added, just to make the next 5 lessons easier for me to add.  Building a large and complex game requires understanding of code and the developer needs to know where to find every method, every variable.  There is an important distinction between "hey Claude, build me a horse game" and saving a couple hours writing a database. I've spent literally thousands of hours writing code for my passion project.
AI use in the game today consists of time-saving things like "add these markings to this list". AI can be useful for debugging, when the root of a problem can be a simple typo that is hard to spot. Bigger debugging problems always require a broader conceptual understanding of the way the game is set up and take human hours to solve. AI has not been used to create any 3D assets, textures, audio, or writing or translations in the game. I cannot guarantee that people I hire to do these tasks do not use AI, as these cooperations are based on trust.
My discord community see behind the scenes and know the care and work that goes into this game. As time goes on I take the gamble that my efforts will produce something that players can enjoy, knowing they are supporting human game developers.

- My accountant may have used a calculator to calculate how much money we lost by releasing 2 games for the price of 1.

name: Celestial DEUS + Aleatores Palace
disclosure:
As a solo developer, transparency with my players is essential to me. That's why I want to clarify that I have used artificial intelligence tools to assist in the creative process of Celestial Deus. Working alone on a project of this scope requires finding creative solutions. AI allowed me to bring my artistic vision to life where my own skills or resources were limited.
Here is how it was used:
Skybox: The skybox, which depicts a stylized sky filled with large clouds as if viewed from a great height, was generated by an AI to match the game's unique atmosphere.

Music: I composed the foundational music tracks myself, and then used AI to remix and enhance them. This gave them more style and complexity for a more immersive ambiance.
My approach was always to use my own creations as a starting point and guide these tools, allowing me to deliver a more complete experience than I could have achieved on my own.

name: life's a beach
disclosure:
Use tilde or j to talk to the chatbot tilde is the console which requires typing say before what you write and j shows a large dialog box with large text. if the robot glitches use tilde to type literally say hello or use j to just write hello. this fixes most glitches with the robot.
the robot contains 72243 patterns. if it loads slightly less than that it should be fine. the reason it may load less is because there is a watchdog used to prevent people from copying the decrypted source code text files that are essentially what the robot uses to respond. on android waiting for the chatbot to fully load its files into memory before interacting with life's a beach seems to work best when wanting to talk to the robot. i've really enjoyed talking to the robot privately when I leave the house and go somewhere.  android pc emulation is really impressive.
im not entirely sure if the robot can process text from non latin character languages english spanish french etc. it may be able to though. even so it will only respond in english. there is an exception to this. if you say your text then add en espanol. the robot will respond with a general response in spanish.
when doing this it won't have access to the wikipedia responses or most information that was added to the robot. the spanish part of the bot was added before chatgpt ever existed.
contains an aiml 2.0 chatbot called brian that generates unique sentences using a dictionary of words and can rarely use an offline wikipedia database to generate sentences.
although udk 3 asks for a firewall exception this is because of achievements and other built in udk 3 features that were difficult to remove.
you access the chatbot completely offline. it loves using ambiguity and in an ordinary dictionary there are words like aborted which can mean cancelled or aborted. the robot as ive run it on my computer loves ambiguity. but the code is determined entirely by the hardware so your robot may work differently than mine.
the robot essentially has no safeguards except it can only generate two sentences and the sentences are random except for sentence structure. the safeguard essentially is it doesn't have swear words or self harm words in it's dictionary and doesn't have wikipedia pages on harmful topics but even if they did they come from wikipedia.
the robot takes words from the first two sentences in a wikipedia article and generates it's own sentence with them or doesn't use them at all although that is unusual.  the only time the robot can swear is when asking about hitler when asked about hitler the robot has the option of calling hitler a swear word.
there is a neat optional feature.
by default the robot only remembers your name between launches of the chatbot when you say my name is. by default he thinks your name is brian. you can allow it to remember more personal information by copying predicates.txt from the life's a beach directory where the bat files are to bots/brian/config.
doing this will allow it to permanently save things like why it likesyou when it decides to do that or whyithatesyou when it decides to do that. these predicates can be updated but now it's possible for it tell you why it likesyou from a previous session.
it also allows the robot to grab sentences it likes from your conversation and save them up to 5. these things happen rarely however so you may never see these things modified within predicates.
at least my computer never wants to say the sentences that trigger the sentences to save.
the robot is completely offline. in fact on android you can infact copy everything within the life's a beach folder to C:/a it doesn't have to have the directory name life's a beach.  you can also access the game completely offline without internet when using gamenative and in fact while using a computer. you can do the exact same thing on steam. however if not launched through steam through the life's a beach directory you will not be able to get achievements as the game will be recognized as the game that inspired this one life in world which was basically the porcupine sex in engine movie sequence the eggs abortion in engine movie sequence the game world as it is now without the challenge areas except it included the sample map that came with udk 3 ie life in world.
the idea being the surrounding map was peaceful while the unreal tournament 3 map was chaotic.
I guess the original idea was animal crossing but your the meme dog that says everything is fine while everything is on fire. but not literally that dog but you get the idea.

Our Philosophy: Human-Led Innovation
A Tool for Artists: This isn't a game made by AI. It's a game made by our team of artists and designers using a new generation of smart tools to build a world we couldn't have even dreamed of a few years ago. All of our 3D game props are hand-crafted. Every key asset, every character, and every story beat starts and ends in the hands of our real hands.
An Ethical & Transparent Approach: We are committed to the ethical use of this technology. That means our AI is guided by human creativity at every step and trained on our own original and ethically-sourced assets, and constantly audited to ensure a fair experience. The privacy and security of your player data is our highest priority.

We create unique experiences:
Store Presence & Character Images: The visuals on our store page were rapidly iterated on with AI tools to find the most compelling composition, all guided by our art director's vision. Living Characters: Every main character has been designed and hand written by our team. We use AI-powered machine learning systems to add richness and variety to the ambient population, making the world feel more realistic and alive without taking focus away from our handcrafted narrative using cutting-edge technology.
The result? A world that feels more alive, characters with more dynamic stories, and an experience that is uniquely yours.
This is the next evolution in gaming and we want you to be a part of it.

disclosure:
AI was used in the creation of certain visual assets, including character avatars, title screen artwork, promotional materials, and background art. However, these assets still required substantial manual work such as design, sketching, outline drawing, and polishing. The AI was used primarily as a tool for coloring and enhancement, and it did not dictate the creative direction. The visual style remains faithful to the original Little Fighter 2.
Some people assume that because AI was used in certain artwork, it must have been applied throughout the entire project. That is far from the truth. I used AI primarily for large-scale visual tasks. To give a clearer picture: the game includes over 3,000 hand-crafted sprite frames, composed from thousands of hand-drawn body parts. In contrast, only about 100 images were AI-assisted, and many of those, such as promotional artwork, don't even appear in the actual game.
I understand that some people may have concerns about the use of AI in the creative process. But I hope people can see the broader context and appreciate the amount of manual effort that went into making this game. Please know that I’m a solo developer working with a limited budget. I’ve been developing this project for around 3.5 years; even quitting my full-time job for a year to work on it full time, without expecting it to cover even half of my previous salary. I've done my best to balance quality and practicality. Your understanding and support mean a great deal to me.

disclosure:
Our Policy for AI Use
Even if, and disclose from time to time that, we use AI in some of our products, it never means that our product consists of AI-generated content, which is simply impossible but may be presumed by some people. We continue our due diligence and necessary efforts to come up with the best content.
AI is a field that we keep track of and welcome curiously and excitedly. It is something not the world gives us but what we get from the world according to our requirements.
However,
We always consider the rights of commercial and ethical use of AI. Therefore, we subscribe to their content, pay their respective fee, and keep their receipts/licenses.
How may we use AI?
We may use outsourced AI in a number of different ways in addition to our own in-game AI mechanics, as it gives us uniqueness and originality as we like, and as long as its content is compliant with our above policy:
Sound files: We have a large collection of audio clips we have purchased and keep purchasing. We also have the means to make our own sound files. Sometimes we may also use AI-made sounds to make audio clips as well if we fail to find what we are looking for in our archive.
Graphics: We may use AI for some of our graphical assets. We have various means like software with which we can create characters, particularly our animated characters in the trailers and cutscenes, which are our own unique designs. We may use AI in this particular game in relation to the environment and some of the ancillary icons, finishings, and corrections.
Ideas: We may chat with AI about whether an idea is suitable for the current genre we are working on. However, we plan to discontinue this use of AI as it lacks originality. For example, when we asked for the names of two female characters for a fantasy game, AI suggested “Anya and Ayleen.” They are obviously names used before and we needed to change the names of our two characters.
The above use of our AI may naturally appear on our store page as we include fragments from our game to introduce and promote it.
This policy may be subject to change depending on the developments, ethical considerations, and circumstances regarding the use of AI in the future.

name: Duskmarch
disclosure:
As a solo developer, I’ve leveraged AI tools to enhance various aspects of Duskmarch’s development while ensuring the game remains a deeply personal and creative project. Specifically, I’ve used AI to assist with the following:
Artwork Creation: AI has been instrumental in generating some of the game’s images, helping me bring the dark fantasy world of Duskmarch to life with visuals that match my vision. These AI-generated assets are carefully curated and often edited to ensure they align with the game’s unique aesthetic.
Text Polishing: To ensure clarity and professionalism, I’ve used AI to correct grammatical and lexical errors in the game’s text, including story content and UI elements. This helps me deliver a polished experience for players.
Localization: AI has also supported the localization process, assisting with translating the game’s stories and interface into multiple languages. This allows me to reach a broader audience while maintaining the integrity of the narrative. All AI-assisted translations are reviewed and refined to ensure accuracy and cultural sensitivity.
While AI has been a valuable tool in streamlining these aspects of development, the core design, storytelling, and gameplay mechanics of Duskmarch are crafted by me, reflecting my passion for creating an immersive and engaging experience. I’m committed to using AI responsibly and transparently, and I’m excited to share this journey with the community!

disclosure:
At Lovely Bytes, we're not just developers, we're passionate gamers like you. And because we understand the gamer's perspective, we firmly believe that the heart of a truly great game lies in the emotional depth and authenticity that only human creativity can provide.
In the development of UNHEIM, artificial intelligence plays a supporting role to accelerate our production, and is used mindfully to help us with certain time-consuming tasks, such as visual brainstorming, or speeding up the process of creating some of the textures. Additionally, AI bravely tackles the Herculean task of turning our chaotic creative thoughts and wild brainstorming scribbles into something resembling coherent, actionable documents.
Our approach to AI is to use it as a tool to augment our skills and capabilities, not to substitute the craft elements that are crucial for creating a deeply engaging and memorable game experience.
Now go and have fun getting scared to death, knowing that what you experience is the result of a mindful blend of assistive technology and traditional craftsmanship.

name: The Path of Veins
disclosure:
All of the images in this game are generated by neural networks trained on images (aka “AI generated”). If you choose to boycott all AI generated material, please do not buy this game. If you are uncomfortable with the thought but are interested in my game, please read on.
The aesthetic of this game had to come from the strange, uncanny look of AI. There is a heartlessness to the visuals that is intentional. I am not trying to copy the look of other artists. The only tool capable of producing the look I was going for was a malfunctioning AI. Ironically, I have had a number of people tell me that it looks much more realistic than standard AI. I am assuming this is because of how I tried to reproduce the look of old media.
All images, aside from the title screen, credits and some of the video shot on camcorder were generated by AI prompts. It took several days of exploring before I began generating images that fit the aesthetic I was looking for. I have heard AI described as a slot machine, and I think the metaphor is somewhat accurate. I think of this as similar to indeterminacy in music. Using random number generators can produce interesting outputs, but you need to refine and direct the system to do so.
I started my process in Midjourney. My ratio of usable images was around 100 to 1; for every 100 images I generated, I found one usable piece for the game. I created an automated process to transform these images to 16:9 widescreen in Photoshop Beta. Some of these images I touched up manually or regenerated sections of the image. There are some real images and hand painted imagery within the AI elements. Often, I would have to generate the sides of the image multiple times because photoshop didn’t generate what I needed.
To those concerned about not paying artists: I understand this, but I want to be clear that this was not created to replace the work of artists, any more than the synthesized scores to horror films were about replacing orchestras. These are tools that do different things. Rather than some sort of lazy shortcut, the use of AI imagery is essential to the aesthetic and narrative of the Path of Veins.

This project was initiated in September 2022. As part of an academic exploration of emerging technologies, AI image generation tools (which were still in the early stages of development at the time) were used to assist with the visual processing of certain content, and an AI music generation tool was used in the production of the background music.
To avoid the misuse of generative AI tools, only the default datasets provided by the respective tools were used during development. The methods of use included:
1. Processing real photographs to create "alien" or "distorted" visual effects;
2. Using abstract images generated from provided keywords as references for manual redesign, reconstruction, and painting;
3. Generating atmospheric music clips by adjusting parameters such as instrumentation and tempo, followed by manual editing and refinement.
All content involving artificial intelligence was completed before 2023. Since then, the use of AI image generation technology in development has been fully discontinued and will not continue in future production.
For all AI-generated image assets used in this work, only usage rights are retained by the project.

disclosure:
# AI Usage in Our Game
In our game, we have utilized generative artificial intelligence (AI) technology to enhance certain aspects of the visual experience. Specifically, we have employed AI-powered tools to assist in the creation of some background images and textures.
Key points about our AI usage:
1. **Pre-rendered Content**: The AI-generated elements are pre-rendered during the development process. This means that the images you see in the game are not being created in real-time as you play.
2. **Limited Scope**: AI has been used primarily for non-essential background elements and textures. All main characters, story-critical environments, and core gameplay elements are hand-crafted by our artists.
3. **Human Oversight**: While AI tools have been used to generate initial ideas or base images, our art team carefully reviews, edits, and refines all AI-assisted content to ensure it meets our quality standards and fits seamlessly into the game's aesthetic.
4. **No Live Generation**: Our game does not use AI to generate any content during gameplay. All AI-assisted elements are fixed and do not change dynamically.
5. **Copyright Compliance**: We have taken great care to ensure that all AI-generated content is original and does not infringe on existing copyrights. Our use of AI tools is in compliance with their terms of service and licensing agreements.
We believe that the thoughtful use of AI in our development process has allowed us to create richer, more detailed environments for players to explore, while maintaining the artistic integrity and vision of our game. As always, we welcome player feedback and are committed to providing a high-quality gaming experience.

disclosure:
In our game development process, we have adopted AI technology to generate art content, mainly for the character portraits of esports players and illustrations in game events. We hope to provide players with richer and more diverse character portraits, but considering the economic, manpower, and time aspects, we find it difficult to afford a large amount of hand-drawn content. We have tried to separate parts such as the mouth, face, and nose, and then assemble them into 3D characters, but the effect was not satisfactory.
Therefore, we decided to try a new method: using AI to generate these contents. We used some of the content we had created before to train the AI model, allowing it to learn and understand the art style and requirements we want. Now, all the AI-generated character portraits and illustrations in the game are made by our trained model, and after completion, we also manually correct them.
We deeply understand that AI cannot replace the creativity and uniqueness of real artists. For this, we feel very sorry, but we also promise you that “Esports Godfather” is not a work without sincerity. We have spent a tremendous amount of time polishing innovative gameplay and various experience content. In these four and a half years, we have been committed to completing a work that satisfies everyone.
We hope you can understand our decision and continue to support our game. We will continue to work hard to provide you with a better gaming experience.

disclosure:
In our game development process, we have adopted AI technology to generate art content, mainly for the character portraits of esports players and illustrations in game events. We hope to provide players with richer and more diverse character portraits, but considering the economic, manpower, and time aspects, we find it difficult to afford a large amount of hand-drawn content. We have tried to separate parts such as the mouth, face, and nose, and then assemble them into 3D characters, but the effect was not satisfactory.
Therefore, we decided to try a new method: using AI to generate these contents. We used some of the content we had created before to train the AI model, allowing it to learn and understand the art style and requirements we want. Now, all the AI-generated character portraits and illustrations in the game are made by our trained model, and after completion, we also manually correct them.
We deeply understand that AI cannot replace the creativity and uniqueness of real artists. For this, we feel very sorry, but we also promise you that “Esports Godfather” is not a work without sincerity. We have spent a tremendous amount of time polishing innovative gameplay and various experience content. In these four and a half years, we have been committed to completing a work that satisfies everyone.
We hope you can understand our decision and continue to support our game. We will continue to work hard to provide you with a better gaming experience.
